questions.sectionHeading: Section I — Common Module: Literary Worlds
questions.stem:
Read Text 1 on page 3.
Compose a discursive response in which you extend the ideas in Text 1.
In your response, articulate your insights into how texts make meaning through the crafting of literary worlds.
questions.stimulus: Text 1: an extract from Ken Liu, The Paper Menagerie and Other Stories. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it on page 3 of the 2025 HSC English Extension 1 paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2026-02/2025-hsc-english-extension-1.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate an understanding of the ideas and values of Literary Worlds and how they are shaped and reflected in texts
craft a sustained composition appropriate to the question, demonstrating control of the use of language

criteria.text: Provides a response that extends the ideas in Text 1 in sophisticated ways; Demonstrates sophisticated insights into how texts make meaning through the crafting of literary worlds; Demonstrates sophisticated control of language and discursive form

Provides a response that extends the ideas in Text 1 in highly effective ways; Demonstrates highly effective insights into how texts make meaning through the crafting of literary worlds; Demonstrates highly effective control of language and discursive form

Provides a response that extends the ideas in Text 1 in sound ways; Demonstrates sound insights into how texts make meaning through the crafting of literary worlds; Demonstrates sound control of language and discursive form

Provides a response that extends the ideas in Text 1 in limited ways; Demonstrates limited insights into how texts make meaning through the crafting of literary worlds; Demonstrates limited control of language and form
Attempts to respond to the ideas in Text 1; Attempts to provide insights into how texts make meaning; Attempts to control language and form

questions.stem:
Read Text 2.
How does Text 2 shape your understanding of the ways your texts ‘creatively break’ dominant assumptions in the elective you have studied?
In your response, make close reference to TWO prescribed texts from your elective and ONE other text of your own choosing.
The prescribed texts for Section II are listed on pages 5−9.
questions.stimulus: Text 2: an extract from Rebecca Solnit, Break the Story. The extract is copyright and is not reproduced here; read it in the 2025 HSC English Extension 1 paper: https://www.nsw.gov.au/sites/default/files/noindex/2026-02/2025-hsc-english-extension-1.pdf
assessedOn: demonstrate an understanding of the ideas and values of Literary Worlds and how they are shaped and reflected in texts
craft a sustained composition appropriate to the question, demonstrating control of the use of language

criteria.text: Provides a sophisticated argument about how Text 2 shapes an understanding of the ways texts ‘creatively break’ dominant assumptions in the elective studied; Demonstrates a sophisticated ability to support their argument through close reference to two prescribed texts from their elective and one other text of their own choosing; Demonstrates a sophisticated control of language and form

Provides a highly effective argument about how Text 2 shapes an understanding of the ways texts ‘creatively break’ dominant assumptions in the elective studied; Demonstrates a highly effective ability to support their argument through close reference to two prescribed texts from their elective and one other text of their own choosing; Demonstrates a highly effective control of language and form

Provides a sound argument about how Text 2 shapes an understanding of the ways texts ‘creatively break’ dominant assumptions in the elective studied; Demonstrates a sound ability to support their argument through close reference to two prescribed texts from their elective and one other text of their own choosing; Demonstrates a sound control of language and form

Provides a limited argument about how Text 2 shapes an understanding of the ways texts ‘creatively break’ dominant assumptions in the elective studied; Demonstrates a limited ability to support their argument through close reference to texts; Demonstrates a limited control of language and form
Attempts to respond to the question; Attempts to support an argument with reference to texts; Attempts to control language and form
